scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The modern form of Umhlanga was established in Eswatini in the 1940s under King Sobhuza II, evolving from the ancient 'umcwasho' custom.
In South Africa, the ceremony was reintroduced in 1991 by King Goodwill Zwelithini to encourage sexual abstinence among young women.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The ceremony is an annual event held in late August or September.
Its official purpose is to preserve female chastity, provide tribute labor for the Queen Mother, and foster solidarity among women.
Today it is a living tradition.

In Eswatini, it is called Umhlanga and held at Ludzidzini.
